home.title: A game built for long routes.
home.intro: Learn Ko Shogi, reconstructed from the 1770 Kōshōgifu and its 1773 commentary. Trace compound turns, fire across the lines, and keep a command condition alive.
home.profile: This is a documented reconstruction. The surviving sources do not establish one most-popular ruleset.
home.noSave: Start a new game to create a local save.
home.sourceNote: Based on public-domain rules texts; no archive images or modern diagrams are reused.
home.footer: An independent strategy game · English v1

tutorial.title: Learn the field
tutorial.intro: Eleven short lessons introduce the source profile and every digital choice. Every move exercise is checked by the same rules engine as a game.
tutorial.wrong: That turn does not match the exercise.
tutorial.movePrompt: Play the complete turn on the board.

content.item003: Meet the reconstructed 1770 setup and its first-move convention.
content.item004: Ko Shogi, reconstructed rules, uses the 19 by 19 formation transcribed from the 1770 Kōshōgifu. Each side begins with 90 pieces across seven ranks. This product uses Black-first as a digital choice because the surviving setup text does not say who starts. No pieces are held in hand or dropped.
content.item005: Who moves first in this product’s reconstructed profile?
content.item006: Black, as an explicit digital convention.
content.item007: White, because every historical rules book says so.
content.item008: The player who has fewer pieces.
content.item009: The setup source leaves first move unspecified; this product labels its choice.
content.item010: The files run from a to s and the ranks from 1 to 19. White advances toward higher ranks; Black advances toward lower ranks. A complete route, its shots, captures, effects and promotion all resolve as one turn.
content.item012: Use the field key to learn every starting and promoted movement form.
content.item013: Each seal has a complete movement entry in the Field Key. It lists all 34 starting types and 23 distinct promoted forms, including each of the 31 promotion assignments. Select any seal to compare its move profile and promotion path. A piece’s profile is authoritative even when two seals share the same movement.
content.item014: What does the Field Key contain?
content.item016: Every starting form, promoted form and promotion path.
content.item017: A history of the source manuscripts only.
content.item018: Use the Field Key to read the full 34-form setup and its promotions.
content.item021: Trace a complete compound route before the turn is committed.
content.item022: Some pieces can make several movement legs before the turn ends. A Master-at-Arms may make up to two Clerk moves, and a Sumo may turn after its first step. Every landing is part of one atomic route. Choose the complete route, not just the first landing.
content.item023: Move the Master-at-Arms from e5 through f6 to g7.
content.item024: The UCI route records the first landing and then the final landing.
content.item026: A shot starts from the piece’s landing point after it moves.
content.item027: A shooter completes its movement first, then chooses a target from the new point. A Longbow can fire up to three intersections along a clear line. The UI asks for the movement and shot as one turn. Shields, Chariots, most shielded vehicles and Five-li Fogs cannot be hit by a Longbow shot.
content.item028: Move the Longbow from e5 to f6, then shoot the Pawn at h8.
content.item029: The @h8 part attaches a shot taken after the move to f6.
content.item031: Ordinary pieces can screen a Cannon shot; fortress pieces stop it.
content.item032: A Cannon’s shot can pass over ordinary pieces. Shield Units and Heavenly Fortresses stop the ray. A Cannon moves before it fires, so the screen and target are measured from its new landing point.
content.item033: Move the Cannon e5–f6. Fire through the Pawn at g7 to capture the Pawn at h8.
content.item034: The Pawn is an ordinary screen. A Shield Unit or Heavenly Fortress would stop this shot.
content.item035: Which piece blocks a Cannon shot?
content.item037: A Shield Unit or Heavenly Fortress.
content.item039: The Cannon passes ordinary pieces but not those two fortress forms.
content.item042: Enter the six-rank camp or earn an automatic promotion by capture.
content.item043: An eligible base piece may promote when its completed route enters, leaves or stays inside the enemy’s six-rank camp. Camp promotion is optional; the choice happens after the whole route. Some captures promote immediately: capturing a command piece, a listed one-step target, or a Frankish Cannon with a Cavalryman triggers the rule.
content.item044: Move the Aide from m13 into White’s enemy camp at m14 and choose Town Brigade.
content.item045: Finish the move first, then choose whether to take the camp promotion.
content.item046: Capture the Middle Troop with the Clerk. The merit rule promotes it automatically.
content.item047: A command-piece capture is a special, automatic promotion trigger.
content.item049: Priest loss restricts Banner and Drum promotion and reverts their flag forms.
content.item050: The Taoist Priest and Spiritual Monk form one Priest family for this convention. Capturing either one permanently blocks that side’s future Banner or Drum promotion, and any promoted Flag Waver or Thunderclap reverts. Banner-and-Drum can supply both command roles while it remains on the board; its special substitution is not undone by Priest loss.
content.item051: Capture the Taoist Priest at e5 with the Chariot Unit. Watch the Flag Waver and Thunderclap revert.
content.item052: Capturing either Priest family piece triggers the lasting restriction and both reversions.
content.item053: What does Banner-and-Drum contribute while it remains on the board?
content.item054: It fills both the Banner and Drum roles.
content.item055: It loses both roles when either Priest is captured.
content.item056: It gives every Pawn two moves.
content.item057: The source profile lets the hybrid provide both command roles.
content.item060: Every arrival burns neighboring pieces of either color.
content.item061: When a Poison Flame arrives at a point, every other piece on an adjacent intersection is removed—friend or foe. This burn follows each landing of a compound route. Any shot or capture on the same completed action is recorded with the whole turn.
content.item062: Move the Poison Flame from e5 to e6 and burn the Pawns at f6 and e7.
content.item063: The effect reaches all eight neighboring intersections.
content.item065: Learn the five-intersection effects and the clear-ray Net restriction.
content.item066: A Five-li Fog suppresses enemy Longbow, Crossbow, Cannon and Frankish Cannon shooting within five king-steps (Chebyshev distance), an explicit reading of an unclear source phrase. The Immaculate Light restores any Fog inside that same distance to a Taoist Priest immediately after a move.
content.item067: How far does a Five-li Fog suppress an enemy shooter in this reconstruction?
content.item071: The chosen digital rule uses Chebyshev distance: five king-steps.
content.item072: Skyward and Earthward Nets immobilize enemies on their unobstructed rays. A piece on a clear ray cannot move. A blocker breaks the ray, so pieces beyond it may move. The exact directions follow each Net’s forward and backward profile.
content.item073: A friendly blocker sits between a Net and an enemy. Does the Net ray reach beyond it?
content.item074: No. The blocker interrupts the ray.
content.item075: Yes, every Net reaches through all pieces.
content.item076: Only if the enemy moves first.
content.item077: The immobilizing ray is stopped by the first piece it reaches.
content.item080: Keep a command condition alive; there is no check rule.
content.item081: A side’s command condition survives with a General, a Governor, or both a Middle Troop and a Banner. Lose when all three conditions are gone. There is no check restriction, no announced check, and no required answer to an attack; the rules let you choose any legal move.
content.item082: Your General is gone, but your Governor remains. Have you lost?
content.item083: No. The Governor alone is still a command condition.
content.item084: Yes. Losing the General always ends the game.
content.item085: Only if the opponent announces check.
content.item086: The Governor is a separate command condition in this profile.
content.item088: A player with no legal action loses; repeated play has defined software outcomes.
content.item089: The player to move has no legal action and neither capture victory nor repetition applies. What happens?
content.item090: That player loses, following the selected digital stalemate convention.
content.item091: The game is automatically a draw.
content.item093: Ko Shogi v1 treats having no move as a loss.
content.item094: The same full position with the same player to move occurring four times is a no-contest draw. Repeating continuous attacks against the opponent’s sole command condition is a loss for the repeating attacker. Other repeated cycles use the digital fourfold-draw convention.
content.item095: A malformed or illegal move is submitted. What does the digital product do?
content.item096: Reject it without changing the position.
content.item099: The product uses casual-play handling: the rejected move leaves the game unchanged.

atlas.title: Field key
atlas.intro: Original seals for all starting and promoted forms. Descriptions follow the selected reconstruction, including its digital conventions.

common.offline: Available offline after the first visit

general.name: General
general.move: One king-step in any direction. Never promotes.

clerk.name: Clerk
clerk.move: One diagonal step, or a jump of exactly two intersections orthogonally.

staff-officer.name: Staff Officer
staff-officer.move: One orthogonal step, or a jump of exactly two intersections diagonally.

sumo.name: Sumo Wrestler
sumo.move: Up to two king-steps in one turn; it may turn after the first. Never promotes.

aide.name: Aide
aide.move: One orthogonal step or one forward-diagonal step.

staff.name: Staff
staff.move: One diagonal step or one forward step.

chief-of-staff.name: Chief of Staff
chief-of-staff.move: One diagonal, forward or backward step.

engineer.name: Engineer
engineer.move: One forward, backward or forward-diagonal step.

taoist-priest.name: Taoist Priest
taoist-priest.move: Jump exactly two intersections in any direction, then optionally shoot one adjacent enemy. Displacement captures only the Priest family.

spiritual-monk.name: Spiritual Monk
spiritual-monk.move: As the Taoist Priest: a two-intersection jump and an adjacent shot; displacement captures the Priest family.

advance-guard.name: Advance Guard
advance-guard.move: Range forward, or one step backward.

middle-troop.name: Middle Troop
middle-troop.move: One king-step in any direction. Can fill one of the paired command roles.

drum.name: Drum
drum.move: One diagonal or sideways step. Its capture removes Pawns’ forward step.

banner.name: Banner
banner.move: One diagonal or sideways step. Can fill one of the paired command roles.

quartermaster.name: Quartermaster
quartermaster.move: Orthogonal range, or one diagonal step.

centuria.name: Centuria
centuria.move: Diagonal range, or one orthogonal step.

rear-guard.name: Rear Guard
rear-guard.move: Range backward, or one step forward.

frankish-cannon.name: Frankish Cannon
frankish-cannon.move: One diagonal step; then up to two shots along any line, at most seven intersections away.

elephant.name: Elephant
elephant.move: Diagonal range in any direction. Never promotes.

longbow.name: Longbow
longbow.move: One diagonal step; then a shot along a clear line up to three intersections away.

crossbow.name: Crossbow
crossbow.move: One diagonal step; then a shot along a clear line up to five intersections away.

cannon.name: Cannon
cannon.move: One diagonal step; then a shot up to five intersections away. Its shot passes ordinary pieces but stops at fortresses.

cavalryman.name: Cavalryman
cavalryman.move: One knight jump. Capturing a Frankish Cannon promotes it.

cavalry.name: Cavalry
cavalry.move: One or two knight jumps. On two jumps, use the same direction or return to the origin.

pawn.name: Pawn
pawn.move: One orthogonal step. Without a friendly Drum, it loses only its forward step.

patrol-unit.name: Patrol Unit
patrol-unit.move: Range forward or backward, or one sideways step.

shield.name: Shield
shield.move: One diagonal step. Longbow-family shots cannot remove it.

shield-unit.name: Shield Unit
shield-unit.move: Sideways range, or one diagonal step. It stops Cannon shots and is immune to every shot.

chariot.name: Chariot
chariot.move: Orthogonal range from one to five intersections. Bow shots cannot remove it.

chariot-unit.name: Chariot Unit
chariot-unit.move: Orthogonal range. Bow shots cannot remove it.

vanguard.name: Vanguard
vanguard.move: Forward range from one to five intersections.

master-at-arms.name: Master-at-Arms
master-at-arms.move: Clerk’s step or jump profile, used for up to two movement legs.

banner-and-drum.name: Banner-and-Drum
banner-and-drum.move: Staff Officer’s profile for up to two legs; supplies both Banner and Drum roles while present.

town-brigade.name: Town Brigade
town-brigade.move: Range forward or backward, or one king-step.

poison-flame.name: Poison Flame
poison-flame.move: Engineer’s steps. Every arrival burns all adjacent pieces of either color.

five-li-fog.name: Five-li Fog
five-li-fog.move: Priest jump and shot, up to two movement legs; suppresses enemy ranged fire within five king-steps.

immaculate-light.name: Immaculate Light
immaculate-light.move: Priest jump and shot, up to two legs; returns nearby Five-li Fogs to Taoist Priests.

skyward-net.name: Skyward Net
skyward-net.move: Backward step, sideways range and forward-diagonal range; immobilizes enemies on clear rays.

governor.name: Governor
governor.move: One king-step in any direction; a second command piece. Never promotes again.

thunderclap.name: Thunderclap
thunderclap.move: Exactly five orthogonal steps with three turns; may capture at each landing.

flag-waver.name: Flag Waver
flag-waver.move: One to five orthogonal steps along one line; may capture along the route.

dragon-ascending.name: Dragon Ascending
dragon-ascending.move: Millenary range or up to two king-steps, turning after the first.

tiger-wing.name: Tiger Wing
tiger-wing.move: Orthogonal range or up to two diagonal steps, with a capture on either.

war-hawk.name: War Hawk
war-hawk.move: Diagonal range or up to two orthogonal steps, with a capture on either.

earthward-net.name: Earthward Net
earthward-net.move: Forward step, sideways range and rear-diagonal range; immobilizes enemies on clear rays.

chariot-of-the-gods.name: Chariot of the Gods
chariot-of-the-gods.move: Orthogonal range from one to five intersections, then the Frankish Cannon’s double shot.

longbow-cavalryman.name: Longbow Cavalryman
longbow-cavalryman.move: One knight jump, then a Longbow shot from the landing point.

crossbow-cavalryman.name: Crossbow Cavalryman
crossbow-cavalryman.move: One knight jump, then a Crossbow shot from the landing point.

gun-carriage.name: Gun Carriage
gun-carriage.move: Orthogonal range from one to five intersections, then a Cannon shot.

winged-horse.name: Winged Horse
winged-horse.move: Up to two knight jumps in any directions.

heavenly-fortress.name: Heavenly Fortress
heavenly-fortress.move: Diagonal range or sideways range. Immune to all shots.
